title: Further Constructions Of Contact Manifolds
notes: Open the lecture as an atlas rather than a single theorem. Chapter 7 is a catalog of manufacturing mechanisms, and the useful habit is to ask what input data enters, what one-form is proposed, what diagnostic proves contactness, and why the construction survives the global operation. The visual names the main recipes so students can orient themselves before formulas arrive.

title: A Reusable Proof Pattern
notes: The chapter repeatedly uses the same four-step proof pattern. Start with a local model, bundle datum, page, or group action. Write down a candidate one-form. Check contact volume, Reeb dynamics, exactness, or a momentum identity. Finally show that the form survives gluing, covering, filling, quotienting, or smoothing. This slide gives students the checklist to reuse.

title: Brieskorn Setup
notes: Introduce Brieskorn manifolds as algebraic links cut out by a weighted complex hypersurface and the unit sphere. The ambient one-form is the standard contact form on the sphere, then the question becomes whether its restriction remains contact on the link. The diagram is intentionally schematic: the sphere supplies compactness, the hypersurface supplies the link, and the one-form supplies the test.

title: Weighted Reeb Flow
notes: The weighted Reeb field is memorable because each coordinate rotates at speed inversely proportional to its exponent. That choice makes the Brieskorn polynomial rotate by a common phase, so the zero set is preserved. The contact check is not a generic sphere argument alone; it uses compatibility between the weighted algebraic equation and the Reeb dynamics.

title: Stein Filling From Smoothing
notes: Move from the link to its filling by replacing the singular fiber with a nearby smooth fiber inside the ball. The plurisubharmonic radius gives a Liouville form, and the boundary carries the induced contact structure. Gray stability explains why small smoothings do not change the contact type unexpectedly. The point is that the algebraic construction comes packaged with a Stein filling.

title: Boothby-Wang Forward
notes: For the forward Boothby-Wang construction, the input is the normalized integral class omega over two pi on the base, with Euler class minus that class. A principal circle bundle with a connection one-form has curvature equal to the pullback of the symplectic form. The contact volume factorizes as the connection form times the symplectic volume downstairs, and the Reeb field is the circle generator.

title: Boothby-Wang Converse
notes: The converse begins with a regular Reeb flow: all orbits are organized as the fibers of a circle bundle. The quotient inherits a symplectic form because d alpha is basic, and the connection form is alpha itself. This is a useful reversal of perspective. Regularity upgrades a dynamical condition on M into a symplectic base whose normalized omega over two pi is integral.

title: Open Book Topology
notes: An open book decomposes the manifold into a binding and pages swept around the binding. The page is a compact manifold with boundary, and the monodromy is the return map used in the mapping torus. The boundary condition that the monodromy is the identity near the boundary is what allows the binding neighborhood to be glued cleanly.

title: Contact Form For An Open Book
notes: The contact form compatible with an open book is built from exact symplectic data on the page and a collar model near the binding. Exact monodromy controls the mapping torus part, while the boundary polar coordinates control the binding. Students should read the two checks together: d alpha is symplectic on each page and alpha is positive along the binding.

title: Bourgeois On M Times T Two
notes: The Bourgeois construction adds two torus directions to a contact manifold supported by an open book. The source convention writes the added terms as x one d theta one minus x two d theta two, with the open-book coordinates supplying x one and x two. The extra terms are not decorative; they supply the missing directions in the contact-volume calculation on M times T two.

title: Fiber Connected Sum
notes: The fiber connected sum is a controlled gluing operation along codimension-two contact embeddings with a fibre-orientation-reversing normal-bundle isomorphism. Standard neighborhoods look like N times a disk with alpha_N plus r squared d theta. Removing tubular neighborhoods and gluing the collars with reversed angular direction lets the contact forms patch after scaling and interpolation.

title: Branched Cover Local Model
notes: The branched covering model p_k sends the normal complex coordinate z to z to the k, and the branch image must itself be a contact submanifold. Pulling back the contact form is good away from the branch locus but degenerates in the normal direction near the branch. The repair term g of r times r squared times gamma restores the missing angular contribution, and taking C large keeps the inherited contact behavior dominant elsewhere.

title: Plumbing Cotangent Disc Bundles
notes: Plumbing builds new exact symplectic domains from cotangent disc bundles using the signed local map from q,p to minus p,q. The canonical one-form is the bookkeeping device: the sign in the pullback is what makes the local symplectic model patch correctly. The contact manifold of interest is then the boundary of the plumbed Liouville domain.

title: Smoothing The Plumbed Boundary
notes: A plumbing creates corners, so the boundary has to be rounded before it is read as a contact manifold. The Liouville vector field gives the check: after smoothing, it remains transverse to the boundary, and the restricted primitive is a contact form. This is the same construction pattern again, now with the survival mechanism being contact type under smoothing.

title: Contact Reduction
notes: For contact reduction, a Lie group acts preserving alpha and the momentum map records alpha applied to infinitesimal generators. The derivative identity follows from Cartan's formula and invariance of alpha. On the zero level, the group directions lie inside the contact hyperplane and the quotient inherits the correct hyperplane distribution when regularity and freeness hypotheses hold.

title: Construction Quality Checklist
notes: Close by turning the chapter into a reusable checklist. For each construction, students should be able to name the input data, the one-form or primitive, the local diagnostic, and the operation that must preserve contactness. This summary also previews how later high-dimensional examples are built: the recipes differ, but the proof obligations remain recognizable.
